evidence.quote: Every application for a review and issuance of a certificate of occupancy as stipulated in § 303-6 of this chapter shall be accompanied by the fees normally required in connection with:
said ordinance was further considered and passed for final adoption at a public hearing held on Thursday, September 17, 2026
Upper Deerfield Township has been prevented from conducting an inspection of properties for the issuance of a Continued Certificate of Occupancy pursuant to township ordinance

Certificate of Occupancy fees were discussed and due to the state requiring two certifications from housing and the Fire Marshall the Committee agreed to introduce an ordinance that will increase the CO fees to $100 if given 5 days or more notice to conduct the inspection or $150 if given 5 days or less.

resale_co.notes: Township Code Chapter 303, Article II (Inspection and Registration of Property) calls for a certificate of occupancy under section 303-6; Ordinance 892 (adopted September 17, 2026, notice of final adoption published September 18, 2026) sets the residential fee by how many business days before closing the request is received. The section 303-6 text itself (ecode360 UP0623) could not be opened, so what exactly triggers the certificate is taken from the ordinance's closing-date fee tiers and Resolution 21-66, which describes a Continued Certificate of Occupancy inspection on sales under township ordinance. Ordinance 892 takes effect 'in the time and manner prescribed by law', which for a regular ordinance is normally 20 days after the notice of final adoption (about October 8, 2026); before then the older fee may apply (the February 5, 2026 minutes give the prior fee as $75.00). The February 19, 2026 minutes say the fee rose because the state now requires two certifications, from housing and from the Fire Marshal, so the one CO fee appears to cover both inspections. The same minutes note a CO is required for all rental properties before a tenant moves in. No application form, checklist or validity period is posted. Resolution 21-66 (March 2021) let buyers accept a seller self-certification in place of the Township inspection during COVID; it is not known whether that option is still used. The Housing & Zoning page lists 'Anthony Lamanteer'; the directory of officials lists 'Tony Lamanteer, Jr.' as Housing Officer and Zoning Officer; a different person, Anthony Lamanteer (alamanteer@upperdeerfield.com), sits on the Township Committee.

fire_cert.notes: The Township is the local fire enforcing agency (registry code M). Its smoke/CO certification for 1-2 family sales is tied to the Township's Continued Certificate of Occupancy: Resolution 21-66 treats the smoke detector, CO alarm and extinguisher certification as part of the CCO inspection, and the February 19, 2026 minutes say the new CO fee (Ordinance 892) covers the two certifications from housing and the Fire Marshal. No separate smoke certificate form or fee is posted, so the fees above are the combined CO fees, not a separate fire fee. The 2021 resolution still names the portable fire extinguisher; the state law of February 3, 2025 (P.L.2025, c.19) removed it from the state requirement, and no current Township checklist was found. Contact numbers: the directory of officials and the state directory give 856-455-9591 for Chris Williams; the Fire Safety page gives 856-451-3811 Ext. 143. Upper Deerfield's construction office also serves Deerfield, Fairfield, Greenwich, Hopewell, Lawrence, Shiloh and Stow Creek, but that is construction code work, not fire code enforcement for those towns.
